title: svc01_service_catalog_scope_test.zig (and likely sibling GBL-migration-verifying tests) write unqualified SQL that resolves against tenant_default instead of public, hitting columns/behavior that only exist in public
summary: Discovered while triaging the ~109 pre-existing zig build test-integration failures found during the ISS-0076 (GitHub #335) fix verification. tests/integration/svc01_service_catalog_scope_test.zig uses TestHarness's h.conn (search_path = tenant_default,public, set by helpers.zig's configureTestSearchPath) and issues unqualified `INSERT INTO service_catalog ...` statements. migrations/GBL-078_svc01_service_catalog_scope.sql -- which adds the scope and owner_tenant_id columns the test exercises -- is a GBL-prefixed migration, so (per src/db/migrations.zig) it runs only against public and was never applied to tenant_default. service_catalog exists in both public (with scope/owner_tenant_id, confirmed via psql) and tenant_default (without those columns, confirmed via psql), so the test's unqualified INSERT resolves to the tenant_default copy and fails with 'column scope of relation service_catalog does not exist'. This is the identical root-cause PATTERN as ISS-0076 (GitHub #335) -- a GBL-migration's effect assumed to be visible somewhere it structurally cannot be -- but manifesting in test code targeting the wrong schema, rather than in a migration's own guard.

root_cause.details: TestHarness.init() (tests/integration/helpers.zig) sets search_path to tenant_default,public for its connection so that tenant-scoped business tables resolve without qualification. This is correct for tests targeting genuinely tenant-scoped tables, but svc01_service_catalog_scope_test.zig is specifically testing a GBL (public-only) migration's effect (SVC-01's scope/owner_tenant_id columns), and its unqualified SQL silently resolves to the wrong schema's copy of a same-named table instead of erring loudly or targeting public explicitly. The test was written without accounting for GBL-prefixed migrations' public-only execution scope.

files_to_change: possibly other integration tests exercising GBL-prefixed migrations via TestHarness's tenant-scoped h.conn -- needs a full audit, not yet enumerated

occurrences.context: Discovered while running a git-stash baseline comparison of zig build test-integration to confirm the ISS-0076 fix introduced no regressions; found ~109 pre-existing failures/noisy-errors unrelated to ISS-0076, of which this GBL-migration/tenant-schema test-routing mismatch is one of three identified independent causes (svc01/svc03/svc04 test suites all show this pattern).

prevention: docs/anti-patterns.md already documents 'guarding a migration DO block with to_regclass() against a table only visible under a different schema than the migration runs in' (added for ISS-0076/#335). Add a sibling entry: 'writing unqualified SQL in an integration test that exercises a GBL-prefixed (public-only) migration's effect, while running under TestHarness's tenant_default-first search_path' -- with the fix being to open a direct public-schema connection or explicitly qualify table names as public.<table> in tests that verify GBL-migration DDL.

A CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR / TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR check: any integration test file whose test cases are named after a GBL-prefixed migration's requirement ID should be flagged for schema-qualification review.
